title: dispatch-gates 扫描把调用方传入的 mkdtempSync base 判为 UNRESOLVED
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgTyMahdAdhXSzgy2nt

Filing gate: ① fleet-tool defect, an instrument whose derivation misreads the tree. Source: fleet. Found on p0 #35588 (os-dev-report 7016701837) and filed on the seat's order (repo:objectstack#1, 2026-11-19 17:27Z). ⛔ Not a claim.

Grade: area:fleet · Bug · p2, as the seat graded it. Main is unblocked by reverting #35495, so nothing is red while this waits. What it blocks is the staged-swap fix for #35079 (and #35502).

## Business reason

`os skills install` / `update` cannot stage its writes next to the skills directory and swap them in by rename. That is the fix for #35079, a half-written catalog after a failed update. The fix cannot land because the dispatch-gates scratch-dir scan fails main's scheduled full run over it. The scan does not say the site is in-tree and exposed. It says it cannot read the site, and its completeness rule treats an unreadable `mkdtempSync` base as a failure. Under `instrument-discipline.md` this is the "推导失真" (derivation distortion) class: `dispatch-gates.mjs` may be touched for it, but the gate's owner has to decide the reading.

## What happens

`applySkillsWrite(dir, …)` in `packages/cli/src/utils/skills-install-state.ts` (as landed by #35495, `578d3b1d66`) calls `mkdtempSync(join(dir, SKILLS_STAGING_PREFIX))`. `dir` is the caller's skills directory, `resolveSkillsDir(args.dir, cwd)` in `skills-command.ts`, which resolves relative to cwd. The scan in `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (`scratchDirSitesInSource` / `resolvePathExpression`, about lines 8700–9300) reads one file at a time and treats a cwd-relative path as unreadable on purpose. The self-test case "no mkdtempSync site in this tree takes a base the scan cannot read" then fails: `UNRESOLVED: packages/cli/src/utils/skills-install-state.ts:246 (dir is not bound in this file)`, 1 of 2564 cases (run 44563404478 at `97f34203`).

The dev ran nine spellings through the scan's own exported `scratchDirSitesInSource`, one substitution each on the real file:

| # | Spelling | Case |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | one-call-site wrapper (parameter hop) | FAIL, UNRESOLVED |
| 2 | a named base constant | FAIL, UNRESOLVED |
| 3 | base derived from the record path | FAIL, UNRESOLVED |
| 4 | `resolve(process.cwd(), dir)` in this file | FAIL, UNRESOLVED |
| 5 | `dir \|\| tmpdir()` (a tmpdir marker the path never takes) | PASS, a lie |
| 6 | a fabricated file-wide `const dir = join(tmpdir(), …)` | PASS, a lie |
| 7 | `mkdirSync` with a random tail | PASS, evades the completeness rule |
| 8 | an aliased `mkdtempSync` import | PASS, invisible to the scan |
| 9 | the site moved to `skills-command.ts` | FAIL (`isAbsolute(chosen) ? chosen : resolve(cwd, chosen)`) |

No honest spelling passes, and every passing spelling is a disguised exemption, so #35588 was closed by reverting #35495.

## Expected

The scan judges a directory-creating call whose base is a caller's argument with a reading the owner chooses, and the reading is honest both ways. Two candidates, for the gate owner to rule:

- **A judged category for a caller-supplied base.** For example, follow the base across the call to its producer, and when that producer is cwd-relative, classify the site under a stated policy (e.g. require an ignore rule over the created prefix at every in-tree root the CLI can be run from) instead of UNRESOLVED.
- **Hold the `mkdtempSync` completeness rule to the population it was calibrated on**, the in-tree test fixtures (the measurement in the scan's own header: 359 sites, 4 in-tree fixtures), and judge production code paths such as this one by the declared-shape net the `mkdirSync` half already uses.

⛔ Either way the scan must not get greener by spelling. Variants 7 and 8 show the rule can be stepped around today; the reading chosen should close that, not widen it.

## Done when

- The ruling is recorded, and the scan plus its self-test implement it.
- The #35495 staged swap (`578d3b1d66`) re-lands with the self-test green and no disguised spelling, and #35079 / #35502 unblock.

## Out of scope (noted here, not filed separately, on the seat's order)

- The site really can land in-tree. A run killed at this repo's root leaves `.claude/skills/.objectstack-skills-staging-*`, and no tracked ignore rule covers it (`git check-ignore -v --no-index` answers `::`). A ruling under the first candidate would require that rule.
- The completeness claim covers the spelling `mkdtempSync` only. Async `mkdtemp(join(PKG, 'tmp', …))` builds in-tree fixture roots the scan never sees (`packages/cli/src/utils/graft-runtime-hooks.test.ts:236`, `packages/cli/test/next-steps.test.ts:83`). Both are covered today by `.gitignore:55` `tmp/`, so nothing is exposed.

Who acts: the owner of `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` (area:fleet).
Dedupe: `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue is:open mkdtempSync scratch scan UNRESOLVED` (filed 2026-11-19 17:3xZ); related only #35588 (the p0 this unblocks), #35079, #35502.
